# A combinatorial interpretation of symmetric-group character-table row sums

<!-- Generated by MathResearchLab. This file is rewritten on every sync; edit the app, not this file. -->

**Status:** Open per source; openness not yet verified

## Statement

Original wording (verbatim from the source):

```latex
The sum has one term per conjugacy class, without class-size weights. The problem asks for a combinatorial interpretation of $R(\lambda)$.
```

Normalized:

Give an explicit family of finite combinatorial sets $\mathcal T(\lambda)$ such that for every integer $n\geq1$ and every $\lambda\vdash n$, $|\mathcal T(\lambda)|=R(\lambda)=\sum_{\rho\vdash n}\chi^\lambda(\rho)$.

Source: Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge, *PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models*, arXiv:2611.33966, p. 16, Appendix A, Problem statements

## Definitions

- **$\chi^\lambda(\rho)$**: The value of the irreducible character of $S_n$ indexed by $\lambda$ on any permutation of cycle type $\rho$. Each partition $\rho\vdash n$ indexes one conjugacy class and contributes once.

## Known results

- $R(\lambda)$ is the multiplicity of $V^\lambda$ in the conjugation action on $\mathbb C[S_n]$. For hook partitions the paper reconstructs a positive counting formula using cycle centralizers. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.3, Proposition B.3.1, p. 31, and B.6.1, p. 41))*
- For a partition $(n-k,\nu)$ with $\nu\vdash k$, the fixed-tail formula gives exact evaluation in $\exp(O(\sqrt{k}))\operatorname{poly}(n)$ bit operations. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.3.2, Theorem B.3.2, p. 33))*
- In a restricted tableau expansion, a lookup matching paired all 50 negative objects with distinct positive objects. The learned rule had five excess collisions on the held-out test partitions. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.3.1, Tables 17–18, p. 32); computational; reproduced: None)*
- Appendix C reports an unsigned matching count for all shapes and direct rules for hooks and two-row shapes. The all-shape construction uses an algebraic argument and has no established efficient membership test. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (Appendix C, Table 22, p. 46))*
